verse: You shall be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God. You shall no more be termed forsaken, and neither shall your land be termed desolate. (Is 62:3-4)
For as a young man marries a young woman, your builder shall marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so will your God rejoice over you. (Is 62:5-6)

He became their savior in all their afflictions. It was not an angel or messenger but his presence that saved them. In his love and in his pity, he redeemed them; he bore them up and carried them all the days of old. (Is 63:9)
The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness. (Lam 3:22)
Can a woman forget her infant, so as not to take pity on the child of her womb? But even if she would forget, still I shall never forget you. (Is 49:15)
Behold, I have engraved you on my hands. Your walls are always before my eyes. (Is 49:16)
Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. (Matt 28:20)
Whoever who comes to me I will never turn away. (Jn 6:37)
You have been forsaken and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you to be an everlasting glory, a joy from generation to generation. (Is 60:15)
The Lord is faithful in all his words, and holy in all his works. The Lord lifts up all who are falling and raises up all who are bowed down. (Ps 145:13-14)
Though the Lord may give you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, yet your teacher will no longer hide himself, but your eyes shall see your teacher. (Is 30:20)

If the world hates you, know that it hated me before it hated you. If you belonged to the world, it would love you as its own. Because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world—therefore the world hates you. (Jn 15:18-19)
How precious is your steadfast love, O God! The children of mankind may take refuge in the shadow of your wings. (Ps 36:7)
God has said, “I will never leave you or abandon you.” (Heb 13:5)
Many are the sorrows of the wicked, but steadfast love surrounds those who trust in the Lord. (Ps 32:10)
Abide in me as I abide in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, so neither can you unless you abide in me. (Jn 15:4)
As the Father has loved me, so I have loved you; Remain in my love. (Jn 15:9)
I in them and you in me, so that they may be completely one, and so that the world may know that you sent me and that you love them just as you love me. (Jn 17:23)
Behold, the hour is coming, and indeed has come, when each of you will be scattered to his own home, and you will leave me alone. Yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me. (Jn 16:32)
The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me to lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside still waters; he restores my soul. He leads me in right paths for his name’s sake. (Ps 23:1-3)
Even if my father and mother forsake me, the Lord will take me up. (Ps 27:10)
Because you are precious in my eyes, and honored, and I love you, I give people in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life (Is 43:4)
For the sake of my servant Jacob, and Israel my chosen one, I have called you by your name, I have surnamed you, though you have not known me. (Is 45:4)

For a brief moment, I abandoned you, but with great mercies, I will gather you. In a moment of indignation, I have hidden my face from you, for. But with everlasting love, I will have mercy on you, says your Redeemer, the Lord. (Is 54:7-8)
Even to your old age I am he, and even to your gray hairs I will carry you. I have made, and I will bear; I will carry, and I will save. (Is 46:4)
Remember, I am with you and will watch over you wherever you go. (Gen 28:15)
Instead of your shame you will have double, instead of dishonor they shall rejoice in their lot. Therefore they shall possess a double portion; everlasting joy shall be theirs. (Is 61:7)
The Lord himself goes before you and will be with you. He will never leave you nor abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged. (Deut 31:8)
You are my hiding place; you will protect me from trouble and surround me with glad songs of deliverance. (Ps 32:7)
The Lord your God is with you; a warrior who gives you victory. The Lord will take delight in you, and in his love he will renew you. (Zeph 3:17)
The Lord waits, so that he may take pity on you. And therefore, he will rise up to show mercy on you. For the Lord is the God of judgment. Blessed are all those who wait for him. (Is 30:18)

I will take you to be my wife forever; I will take you to be my wife in righteousness, justice, steadfast love, and in compassion. I will betroth you to me in faithfulness; and you shall know the Lord. (Hos 2:19)

Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man. Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, for your reward is great in heaven (Luk 6:22-23)
The Lord loves justice: he will not abandon his faithful ones. They are preserved forever, but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off. (Ps 37:28)
Those who know your name put their trust in you, for you, O Lord, have not forsaken those who seek you. (Ps 9:10)
For the Lord will not forsake his people for his great name’s sake, because it has pleased the Lord to make you his people. (1 Sam 12:22)
It is I, I myself, who will comfort you. Why then would you be afraid of a mere mortal who must die, a human who will wither like the grass? (Is 51:12)
I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth. And I will raise up for you an everlasting covenant. (Eze 16:60)
Thus says the Lord who created you, O Jacob, and who formed you, O Israel: Do not be afraid. For I have redeemed you, and I have called you by your name. You are mine. (Is 43:1)
He never withdraws his mercy from us. Although he chastises us with adversity, he does not forsake us. (2 Mac 6:16)
Take courage, O Jerusalem, for he who has named you, will comfort you. (Bar 4:30)
The beloved of the Lord will dwell in safety; and the Lord will surround him all day long, and he will rest between his shoulders. (Deut 33:12)
By this we know that we dwell in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. (1 Jn 4:13)
For the mountains may depart and the hills be removed, but my steadfast love will not depart from you, neither will the covenant of my peace be removed. (Is 54:10)
As a father is compassionate to his children, so has the Lord been compassionate to those who fear him. For he knows how we were formed. He remembers that we are dust. (Ps 103:13-14)
I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore with loving kindness have I drawn you. (Jer 31:3)

I am certain that neither death, nor life, nor Angels, nor Principalities, nor Powers, nor the present things, nor the future things, nor strength, nor the heights, nor the depths, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. (Rom 8:38-39)
The eye has not seen, and the ear has not heard, nor has it entered into the heart of man, what things God has prepared for those who love him. (1 Cor 2:9)

I passed by you and saw you. And behold, you were at the age of love. And I spread my garment over you, and I covered your nakedness. And I swore to you, and I entered into a covenant with you, says the Lord God, and you became mine. (Eze 16:8)
As a mother comforts her child, so will I comfort you. And you will be comforted in Jerusalem. (Is 66:13)
